name: How do you know if a pool should be removed or repaired?

mainEntity.name: How can a homeowner tell whether an old in-ground pool should be removed instead of repaired or resurfaced?
mainEntity.text: How can a homeowner tell whether an old in-ground pool should be removed instead of repaired or resurfaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision comes down to repair cost, long-term usefulness, and the condition of the structure. If the shell is cracked, plumbing leaks keep returning, equipment is outdated, or the finish and deck need major work, removal may be smarter than another round of repairs. If the pool is structurally sound and still fits the family’s lifestyle, renovation could be the better investment. Homeowners should compare the all-in cost of repair against the cost of removal plus yard restoration. In Los Angeles, this question often comes up when owners want to modernize the property rather than keep maintaining an aging pool. A contractor can inspect access, pool construction type, and site conditions, but the best decision also depends on how the yard will be used in the next five to ten years.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pool may be a better removal candidate if the shell is cracked, plumbing leaks are recurring, equipment is obsolete, or repair costs are approaching replacement-level money. If the structure is sound and the homeowner still wants a pool, repair may be more sensible. A site inspection should compare repair cost, remaining lifespan, and future use.
